Earlier this summer, Apple hiked prices significantly due to the ongoing global memory crisis. Examples include the iPad Air going from $599 to $749, the M5 MacBook Pro from $1,699 to $1,999, and the Apple TV from $129 to $199. The above are just some examples — the key point is that the magnitude of this round of price increases is quite staggering.

This raises a question — will Apple make bold improvements to its products so that they remain attractive at their new prices?

Of course, some Apple products are about to undergo major revamps, with the MacBook Pro and iPad mini being two of them. However, for products without significant updates, I don't think Apple can sell last-generation technology at much higher prices while still making people feel it's worth buying — especially compared to the current state of the second-hand market.

If you could buy an M4 iPad Air for $599 (or even as low as $499) a few months ago, why would you want to pay $749 now? The higher the price, the more obvious this contradiction becomes.

Some Apple products haven't seen major changes for a long time. The iPad Air has used the same design and feature set since 2020, with only chip upgrades and Apple Pencil Pro support added during that period. The base-model iPad has largely remained the same from 2022 to now, and the iMac has been the same from 2021 to now as well.

Do these products need a complete redesign? Not necessarily. But I think Apple could do something to make them more appealing at their current prices. For example, putting a miniLED display on the iMac, upgrading the iPad Air to 120Hz, and giving the base-model iPad a fully laminated display.

Compared to price increases, the cost of these upgrades is relatively low, but should make consumers feel much more comfortable paying the new prices. Conversely, Apple may also lower the specifications of some products to offset the price hikes. For example, the iPhone may return to 128GB of storage.

What do you think of Apple's product lineup after the price increases? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
